claims.text: CHECKLIST A.1 — replay post-merge, independently of the original author's run: DONE. test_e11_authority_gate.py replayed by ARM-06 at the canonical cwd, exit 0, 7/7 cases, 0 bytes stderr, at HEAD c5fa2f8. Producer was not the author of 032d900.

CHECKLIST A.2/A.3/A.4 — boss_stability rejects, world_tick rejects, boss_release_delay remains writable: SATISFIED AGAINST THE REGISTRY DOCUMENT ONLY, each with a demonstrated failure under its own negative control. NOT satisfied as product behaviour: no E11 admission path exists, so nothing rejects anything. This is the distinction L4/L5 must rule on and it is deliberately not blurred.

CHECKLIST A.5 — C10 reads unaffected: OPEN, by explicit ruling and by measurement. counter_threshold occurs 0 times across all 10 implementation surfaces, so 'unaffected' is VACUOUSLY true rather than verified. Expected semantics were not found in canon. No test was invented.

CHECKLIST A.6 — preserve commands, stderr, producer exit codes, hashes, claim-to-evidence links: DONE. 15 envelopes, all ADMITTED by the authoritative validator, every sha256 recomputable, no 2>/dev/null and no bare || true anywhere in the harnesses.

CHECKLIST B.1/B.2 — every retained assertion observed FAILING under a relevant negative control and PASSING under the canonical fixture: DONE. total_hp_lost went 0/5 -> 3/5 sim-rule controls after repair; all six assertions have a demonstrated failure.

CHECKLIST B.3 — remove or replace non-discriminating assertions: DONE, and applied twice. The carried total_hp_lost bound [1, 10_000_000] was replaced with an exact expectation; and a stability guard I wrote MYSELF was removed after proving it could not fail.

CHECKLIST B.4 — characterise the oracle correctly as diagnostic specificity, not detection beyond the hash, and do not overclaim: DONE, with two self-corrections. The hash strictly dominates the oracle as a DETECTOR (state_hash diverged under every control, including two the oracle passes); and my own 'the design, not a gap' sentence was falsified by per-tick measurement showing a ~300-tick blind window.

KESTREL ITEM 5 — exercise one real E11 admission path end-to-end: PENDING ARM-08 by ruling. The control is built and all four of its exit branches are exercised; it exits 2 PRODUCT_AUTHORITY_PATH_ABSENT today and becomes a real authority test with no edit when E11 lands.

KESTREL ITEM 6 — PRODUCT_AUTHORITY_PATH_ABSENT reported rather than a path invented: DONE and ADMITTED. E11 occurs 0 times across 10 implementation surfaces and 7 in specification, with a working detector positive control.

Beyond the checklist: six defects in the E11 gate found and closed, each with a measured before/after exit code — absent-reads-as-denied, positional column capture, exit-code collision, garbled verdict silently denied, write-column removable, and registry drift fail-open. Plus one stale §4.1 read anchor corrected under grant.

ARM STATE IS BLOCKED, not complete. Two exits are sealed by permission denials that no authority grant clears: `git push -u origin arm/product-verification-v1` (25 commits, no upstream) and `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:10086/command` for the Head 06 channel. The checkpoint for Head 06 is written, hash-stable and undelivered.

decisions_requested: Does K-01 close on registry-document evidence plus the PRODUCT_AUTHORITY_PATH_ABSENT proof, or stay ACTIVE pending an implemented E11 admission path?
Is E1-E16 a roadmap or a contract? The design specifies 16 effects; SkillSystem.LEGAL_EFFECTS is ['destabilize_anchor'] — one. That gap is larger than the E11 repair and is not ARM-06 scope.
Does the ~300-tick oracle blind window stay recorded-not-closed under 'minimum means minimum', or is trajectory sampling authorised as a separate bounded item?
risks: STATE IS BLOCKED, NOT COMPLETE_CANDIDATE. COMPLETE_CANDIDATE would be an overclaim: A.5 is OPEN by ruling and Kestrel item 5 is pending ARM-08 by ruling. An arm with items open by its own Head's instruction is not a completion candidate.
All 25 commits and 16 envelopes are reachable only from this worktree. Deleting it destroys the cycle's entire output — the condition that already destroyed one version of the oracle.

Four times this cycle my own tooling was the defect and reported confidently: a ripgrep single-file count, an ERR_MALFORMED admission probe, a git ls-files index audit, and a stability guard that could not fail. Every one was caught by checking a case whose answer was already known. That pattern is the most transferable output of this arm.
